ety.text: Russification of the Armenian Հակոբյան (Hakobyan), by substituting the Armenian ending -յան (-yan) with Russian -ов (-ov).

s.g: Berne (a town in Indiana, United States)
used as a friendly form of address to a man or boy
a surname, Goncharov, originating as an occupation
to fly (to, as far as), (thrown object, projectile etc) to reach
litmus paper (paper containing a water-soluble mixture of different dyes extracted from certain lichens)

ety.text: Borrowed from French miniature, from Italian miniatura, from Latin miniō (“to colour/color red”), from minium (“red lead”).

s.g: inside out, on the wrong side
to throw on, to throw over
there is no need (to), there is no use (to)
guardsman, warrior of a Mongolian khan

ety.text: Attested since the reign of Peter the Great in the military and surgical sense; from Latin operatio, via Polish operacja or German Operation.

s.g: to grin, to smile broadly (showing the teeth)
to drive back/off/away, to press back, to push aside, to shove back
to show oneself, to come in sight, to appear

ety.text: From Proto-Slavic *polьga. Cognates include Ukrainian пільга (pilʹha), Polish ulga.

x: — Кака́я жа́лость, что вы не слу́жите, — сказа́ла она́ доброду́шной жене́ милиционе́ра, кото́рая мы́ла посу́ду.

s.g: container, in which food products or drinks are sold, such as jar, bottle, etc.

ety.text: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *posǫda. For more see су́дно (súdno).

s.g: to disband, to dissolve (an organization or group)

ety.text: From сталь (stalʹ, “steel”) + -е- (-e-) + a deverbal form of вари́ть (varítʹ, “to weld”).
Inherited from Old East Slavic судьба (sudĭba), from судити (suditi, “to judge”) + -ьба (-ĭba) (synchronically, суди́ть (sudítʹ) + -ьба (-ʹba)). Cognate with Old Church Slavonic сѫдьба (sǫdĭba).

s.g: counting rhyme (short rhyme used among children to count through a group and pick someone)
transcendent (lying beyond the limits of experience)
x: — Я всегда удивляюсь ясности и точности выражений вашего мужа, — сказала она. — Самые трансцендентные понятия становятся мне доступны, когда он говорит.

ety.text: Derived from Latin trānscendens + -ный (-nyj), from Latin trānsscendō, from Latin trāns- + Latin scandō (whence also scāla, whence Russian шкала́ (škalá), эскала́тор (eskalátor)).

s.g: to make sure of, to verify
to be convinced of, to be confident of
to kill, to destroy, to make unfit for habitation or growth

ety.text: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic оумрьщвлѣти (umrĭštvlěti). By surface analysis, у- (u-) + мёртвый (mjórtvyj) + -я́ть (-játʹ).

s.g: bread box, bread bin (a container for storing bread)

ety.text: хлеб (xleb) + -о- (-o-) + Ukrainian -роб (-rob). Compare with Ukrainian хліборо́б (xliborób). The unproductive agent suffix -роб (-rob), identical to Russian -дел (-del) is believed to be of Ukrainian origin.
From я́вств- (jávstv-) + -енный (-ennyj); constructed as if from a nonexistent *я́вство.
Inherited from Old East Slavic ꙗрьмъ (jarĭmŭ), from Proto-Slavic *arьmo, *arьmъ, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂er-.
